findings.title: Cache status ignores expiry, marking stale rows as fresh
findings.body: getCacheStatusByCredentialIds uses prisma.calendarCache.groupBy to find the most recent updatedAt for each credential, but it does not constrain expiresAt to be in the future. The UI displays a 'Cache Status' timestamp whenever a row exists, even when all matching rows are expired (cache TTL is 30 days, set in upsertCachedAvailability via CACHING_TIME). Because getCachedAvailability itself filters by expiresAt >= now, the user is shown what looks like valid cache data for credentials whose cache is actually invalid. Add `expiresAt: { gte: new Date(Date.now()) }` to the where clause so the UI only surfaces still-valid cache.

findings.title: Timestamp hard-coded to en-US locale
findings.body: Inside the cache_status dropdown, the timestamp is rendered with `new Intl.DateTimeFormat("en-US", { dateStyle: "short", timeStyle: "short" }).format(...)`. The component already has access to useLocale() for translations, but forces every user to see dates in the US format regardless of their locale, browser preference, or the locale actually in use in the rest of the app. This is a regression for non-en-US users and breaks the i18n expectations of the project. Use the locale returned by useLocale() (or navigator.language fallback) instead of the hard-coded `"en-US"`.

findings.title: deleteCache success does not invalidate connectedCalendars
findings.body: After deleting the cache the mutation only shows a toast and calls onSuccess?.(); it never invalidates the viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars query. The sibling disconnectMutation on lines 53-65 explicitly invalidates utils.viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars and utils.viewer.apps.integrations on settle, which keeps the dropdown and parent list in sync. The deletion path lacks the same invalidation, so after a successful Delete cached data the dropdown continues to render the 'Cache Status' row with the previous timestamp and the 'Delete cached data' item, and the parent's ConnectedCalendarList still shows the now-stale cacheUpdatedAt. Add an invalidate of utils.viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars (and ideally utils.viewer.apps.integrations) in onSuccess or onSettled.

findings.title: BSD sed syntax breaks on Linux
findings.body: The line `sed -i '' -E "s|^GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL=.*|GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL=$TUNNEL_URL|" "$ENV_FILE"` uses the BSD/macOS form `sed -i ''` where the empty argument is the backup-extension placeholder. On GNU sed (the default on the Linux/CI environments this repo targets), `-i ''` is parsed as `-i` followed by `''` and then `-E`, causing errors like `sed: can't read E: No such file or directory`, so the .env update silently fails and the rest of the script can't restore GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL. Detect the platform (e.g. `[[ $OSTYPE == darwin* ]] && sed_i() { sed -i '' "$@"; } || sed_i() { sed -i "$@"; }`) or use a portable alternative such as `sed -i.bak ... && rm "$ENV_FILE.bak"`.

findings.title: updateManyByCredentialId invoked with empty data
findings.body: `await SelectedCalendarRepository.updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, {});` passes an empty data object, which only does anything because Prisma auto-bumps `@updatedAt`. Without that hidden schema behavior this would be a no-op (or even a validation error in some Prisma versions), so the intent ('bump SelectedCalendar.updatedAt for all calendars under this credential') is implicit and brittle. Pass the timestamp explicitly, e.g. `data: { updatedAt: new Date() }`, and document that the field exists at the call site.

findings.title: deleteCache throws plain Error instead of TRPCError
findings.body: The handler throws `new Error("Credential not found or access denied")` directly. The other handlers in this package throw `TRPCError` with appropriate codes (e.g. NOT_FOUND, UNAUTHORIZED). Throwing a bare Error here skips tRPC's code propagation: the client receives an INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR with a 500 status for what is really a 404 / 403, and the toast in CredentialActionsDropdown cannot distinguish 'not found' from 'permission denied' from a transient DB error. Switch to `throw new TRPCError({ code: "NOT_FOUND", message: "Credential not found or access denied" })`.

findings.title: Migration comment does not match SQL
findings.body: The header comment warns: 'Added the required column `updatedAt` to the `CalendarCache` table without a default value. This is not possible if the table is not empty.' The actual SQL does add a default (`DEFAULT NOW()`), so the warning is wrong and will confuse whoever next reviews this migration or runs it against a non-empty table. Either remove the misleading warning or replace it with one that describes the actual safe approach (adding the column with a server-side default and back-filling existing rows).

findings.title: DropdownMenuItem used for non-interactive cache info
findings.body: The 'Cache Status' / 'Last updated' block (lines 84-97) is rendered inside a `<DropdownMenuItem className="focus:ring-muted">` even though it contains no actionable control - it is purely informational. Radix dropdown items are interactive elements that expect to be selectable, so making one that does nothing on click produces an a11y warning (role with no action/handler) and means a screen-reader user hears it as a menu choice they can activate. Use a non-interactive primitive such as a `<div>` or `<DropdownMenuLabel>` for the read-only cache status row and reserve DropdownMenuItem for the Delete cached data choice below.
